playground/playground/__init__.py::000: This package initializer defines the package version via the __version__ = "0.1.0" variable and re-exports many symbols imported from submodules so they are available at the playground.playground package level. It imports and exposes decorators (AuditTrail), enums (Category, EventType, OrderStatus), the event bus (EventBus), exception classes, inventory (Warehouse), domain models (Customer, LineItem, Money, Product), order-related types (Order, OrderBuilder, OrderLog), pricing strategies (FlatPricing, BulkDiscountPricing), and simulation helpers (Simulation, run_simulation). The __all__ list explicitly controls the public API by listing the names that will be exported when using from playground.playground import *. The file itself performs no validation, side effects, or computations beyond importing and exporting these symbols.
playground/playground/base.py::000: Defines two abstract base classes. Entity declares an abstract identity() method that concrete subclasses must implement to return a unique string key; equality (__eq__) compares identity for objects of the exact same concrete type, __hash__ hashes the concrete type name together with the identity, and __repr__ returns a developer-friendly representation including the identity. PricingStrategy declares an abstract price(items) method to compute a total Money for a sequence of LineItem objects and implements __call__ as a convenience alias that forwards to price. PricingStrategy._sum_subtotals(items) is a static helper that returns Money(0) for empty input or the sum of item.subtotal values (it imports Money lazily) and has no side effects.
playground/playground/base.py::001: Repository is an abstract base class representing a keyed storage of Entity objects. It declares four abstract methods: add(item: Entity) -> None to store an entity by identity, get(key: str) -> Entity to return the entity for a given key and raise KeyError if missing, remove(key: str) -> Entity to remove and return the entity for a key and raise KeyError if missing, and __iter__() -> Iterator[Entity] to iterate stored entities; these must be implemented by subclasses. The concrete __contains__(key: object) -> bool is implemented: it returns False for non-string keys, otherwise it calls get and returns True if no KeyError is raised and False if get raises KeyError. There are no other side effects in this excerpt.
playground/playground/decorators.py::000: Defines a single class, AuditTrail, which is a class-based decorator that records call outcomes into an internal in-memory list. AuditTrail.__init__ validates that label is a non-empty string and raises TypeError or ValueError otherwise, and stores a private entries list. AuditTrail.__call__ validates that the target is callable and returns a wrapper that invokes the function, appends "<label>:<func_name>:ok" on success or "<label>:<func_name>:error:<ExceptionName>" on exception, re-raising the original exception; the wrapper returns the wrapped function's result. The entries property returns an immutable tuple snapshot of recorded entries, clear() removes all entries as a side effect, and __len__ returns the current number of recorded entries.
playground/playground/enums.py::000: Defines three Enum classes. Category represents product categories (ELECTRONICS, GROCERY, APPAREL, HARDWARE), provides Category.from_label(label: str) which normalizes a string and returns the matching Category, raising TypeError if label is not a str and ValueError if no match is found, and overrides __str__ to return the member's value. OrderStatus represents order lifecycle stages (NEW, RESERVED, SHIPPED, CANCELLED) and declares an is_terminal property that is not implemented yet; based on its name/signature/docstring it should return whether a status is terminal (e.g., SHIPPED or CANCELLED). EventType lists integer event topic constants (STOCK_ADDED, STOCK_RESERVED, STOCK_RELEASED, ORDER_SHIPPED, ORDER_CANCELLED).
playground/playground/events.py::000: Defines an EventBus class implementing a synchronous in-process publish/subscribe registry keyed by EventType. EventBus.__init__ initializes an empty dict mapping EventType to lists of handlers. EventBus.subscribe(event_type, handler) validates types (raises TypeError if event_type is not EventType or handler not callable) and appends the handler to the registry. EventBus.unsubscribe(event_type, handler) removes a handler if present and returns a boolean indicating whether removal occurred. EventBus.publish(event_type, payload) validates inputs (raises TypeError for invalid event_type or non-Mapping payload), calls each subscribed handler with the payload, and returns the number of handlers invoked. EventBus.__len__ returns the total number of registered handlers across all event types. EventBus.__contains__ is not implemented yet; based on its name and signature it should check whether a given event_type has any registered handlers (i.e., membership in the bus).
playground/playground/exceptions.py::000: This module defines a small exception hierarchy for the playground package. PlaygroundError is the root exception type and InventoryError subclasses it as a generic inventory failure; both are simple markers (their bodies contain only pass). OutOfStockError(InventoryError) stores sku, requested, and available attributes and constructs a descriptive error message indicating insufficient stock. UnknownSKUError(InventoryError) stores the unknown sku and sets a message noting the unknown SKU. DuplicateEntityError and InvalidTransitionError (both subclasses of PlaygroundError) store a key and a source/target pair respectively and build readable messages describing the duplicate identity or illegal transition.
playground/playground/inventory.py::000: This chunk contains the module docstring and import statements for an inventory ledger and warehouse location module; it does not define any classes or functions in the shown lines. It imports Entity and Repository from .base, three domain exceptions (InvalidTransitionError, OutOfStockError, UnknownSKUError) from .exceptions, and two utility functions (ensure_positive_int, normalize_sku) from .util, along with typing helpers Dict and Iterator. The presence of these imports indicates the rest of the module will work with entities/repositories, validate and normalize SKUs, and raise the listed exceptions for invalid state transitions, unknown SKUs, or out-of-stock conditions. No runtime behaviour, validation, or side effects occur in the provided lines.
playground/playground/inventory.py::001: InventoryLedger manages on-hand and reserved quantities per SKU and is initialized with a Repository used for SKU validation; it raises TypeError if the repository is not a Repository. _require_sku normalises a SKU and raises UnknownSKUError if unregistered. add_stock validates quantity, validates SKU, increments on-hand and returns the new total; available returns on-hand minus reserved. reserve validates inputs, checks availability and raises OutOfStockError if insufficient, increments reserved and returns a ReservationContext; release and commit validate inputs, raise InvalidTransitionError if trying to release/commit more than reserved, and update reserved (commit also decrements on-hand). __contains__ is not implemented yet and should test membership of a SKU (likely normalising and checking registration or on-hand presence). __len__ returns the count of SKUs with positive on-hand stock and __iter__ yields those SKUs in sorted order.
playground/playground/inventory.py::002: ReservationContext is a context-manager class that represents a held reservation of a given SKU and quantity against an InventoryLedger. Its __init__ stores the ledger, sku, quantity and sets an initial state "held"; the state property returns the current state string. __enter__ returns self but raises InvalidTransitionError if the reservation is not in the "held" state. __exit__ returns False and, if the reservation is still "held", calls ledger.release(sku, quantity) and sets the state to "released" (side effect: releases stock on exit). commit() raises InvalidTransitionError if not "held", otherwise calls ledger.commit(sku, quantity) and sets the state to "committed". __repr__ returns a developer-friendly string representation.
playground/playground/inventory.py::003: Defines class Warehouse (subclassing Entity) representing a named location that owns an InventoryLedger. The constructor __init__ validates that warehouse_id is a non-empty string (raising ValueError) and that ledger is an InventoryLedger (raising TypeError), then stores warehouse_id, name and ledger. identity() returns the warehouse_id string; the ledger property returns the associated InventoryLedger object. receive(sku, quantity) delegates to the ledger by calling ledger.add_stock(sku, quantity) and returns that method's integer on-hand total; __repr__ returns a developer-friendly string. stock_report is not implemented yet; based on its name and signature it should return a Dict[str,int] mapping SKUs to on-hand quantities (a stock report) for the warehouse.
playground/playground/models.py::000: Defines a Money class representing an immutable amount stored in integer cents. The constructor validates that cents is an int (not bool) and non-negative, raising TypeError or ValueError as appropriate. Arithmetic and comparison methods are provided: __add__, __sub__ (raises TypeError for wrong type and ValueError if result would be negative), __mul__/__rmul__ (require non-negative int factors), __eq__, __lt__, __le__, and __hash__/__repr__/__str__ (string formatted via format_cents). The __bool__ method is not implemented yet; based on its name and signature it should determine Money truthiness (likely True for nonzero amounts).
playground/playground/models.py::001: Defines a Product class representing a catalog item with attributes sku, name, category, and unit_price, set in __init__ after validation: sku is normalized, name must be a non-blank string (ValueError if missing), category must be a Category and unit_price must be a Money (TypeError otherwise). Read-only properties sku, name, category, and unit_price return those attributes, and identity() returns the SKU. with_price(new_price) returns a new Product with the same SKU, name, and category but the provided Money price, raising TypeError if new_price is not a Money. The classmethod from_dict(data) requires keys "sku", "name", "category", and "unit_price_cents" (KeyError if missing), accepts category as a str (converted via Category.from_label) or a Category instance (TypeError otherwise), builds a Money from unit_price_cents, and returns a Product. The staticmethod is_valid_name(name) returns True only for a string of 1..80 non-blank characters.
playground/playground/models.py::002: LineItem is a value object representing one SKU with a quantity and a unit price. Its constructor validates and normalizes the SKU via normalize_sku, ensures quantity is a positive int via ensure_positive_int, and raises TypeError if unit_price is not a Money instance; it stores sku, quantity and unit_price as private attributes. Read-only properties sku, quantity and unit_price return those values and subtotal returns unit_price multiplied by quantity as a Money value. with_quantity(quantity) returns a new LineItem with the same SKU and unit_price but the provided quantity. Equality compares SKU, quantity and unit_price (returns NotImplemented for other types) and __hash__ hashes by SKU and quantity; __repr__ returns a developer-friendly string.
playground/playground/models.py::003: Defines class Customer(Entity) representing a buyer with a credit limit and an outstanding balance. The constructor validates inputs, raising ValueError if customer_id or name are missing/blank and TypeError if credit_limit is not a Money instance; it sets _customer_id, _name, _credit_limit and initializes _balance to Money(0). Read-only properties customer_id, name, credit_limit and balance return those values, and identity() returns the customer_id. can_afford(self, total: Money) is not implemented yet; based on its name and use it should return True if charging total would not exceed the credit limit (i.e., allow charge), and charge(total) increases the balance by total but first calls can_afford and raises ValueError("credit limit exceeded") if the charge is not permitted.
playground/playground/orders.py::000: OrderStateMachine defines a state-machine for OrderStatus with a TRANSITIONS mapping that lists allowed target statuses for each source status. The static method allowed_from(status) validates that status is an OrderStatus (raising TypeError otherwise) and returns the frozenset of reachable statuses. The instance method can_transition(source, target) returns a boolean indicating whether target is reachable from source by consulting allowed_from. The transition(source, target) method is not implemented yet; based on its name, signature and imports it should perform/validate a state transition (likely raising InvalidTransitionError on disallowed transitions and returning the new status). The __call__ method is a convenience alias that delegates to transition.
playground/playground/orders.py::001: Defines class Order which models a customer order with items, status and pricing. The constructor validates order_id, customer and pricing, raising ValueError for empty id and TypeError for wrong types, and initializes empty line items, status NEW and an OrderStateMachine. Properties expose order_id, customer, status, a tuple snapshot of items, and total (computed by calling the PricingStrategy.price method); add_item validates the argument type, raises TypeError for non-LineItem, raises InvalidTransitionError if order is not NEW, and appends or merges quantities into the internal items list (side effect). advance delegates to the state machine to compute and set a new status (may raise on invalid transitions). Order.__len__ is not implemented yet; based on its name and class it should return the number of line items. Methods __iter__, __eq__, __hash__ and __repr__ provide iteration over items, identity comparison by order_id, a stable hash, and developer-friendly representation.
playground/playground/orders.py::002: Defines the OrderBuilder class, a fluent builder for constructing Order objects for a given Customer and PricingStrategy. Its __init__ validates types and raises TypeError if customer is not a Customer or pricing is not a PricingStrategy, and initializes an internal list of (sku, quantity, unit_price) tuples. The classmethod for_customer(customer) returns a builder using FlatPricing by default. add(sku, quantity, unit_price) creates a LineItem, records its sku, quantity and unit_price into the builder and returns self for chaining. build(order_id) raises ValueError if no lines were recorded, otherwise creates an Order, adds each recorded LineItem to it, and returns the Order. __len__ returns the number of recorded lines and __bool__ is True when at least one line exists.
playground/playground/orders.py::003: OrderLog is an ordered, deduplicated, iterable record of orders. Its __init__ creates an empty internal list, record(order) appends an Order after validating the argument is an Order (raises TypeError otherwise) and rejects duplicates by order_id (raising DuplicateEntityError on duplicate). by_status(status) is not implemented yet; based on its signature it should return an iterator over orders whose status equals the given OrderStatus. __getitem__(index) returns the order at the given index, __len__ returns the number of logged orders, and __iter__ yields the logged orders in insertion order.
playground/playground/pricing.py::000: Defines FlatPricing, a PricingStrategy that computes an order total by summing line item subtotals and applying a flat tax rate expressed in basis points. Its __init__(tax_bps) validates that tax_bps is an int (not bool) and between 0 and 10000, raising TypeError or ValueError on invalid input, and stores it privately. The tax_bps property returns the configured basis-point rate. The price(items) method returns a Money: it obtains a subtotal via _sum_subtotals(items), returns the subtotal unchanged if tax_bps is 0, otherwise computes tax as Money(subtotal.cents * tax_bps // 10000) and returns subtotal + tax.
playground/playground/pricing.py::001: Defines class BulkDiscountPricing, a subclass of PricingStrategy that wraps another PricingStrategy and applies a percentage discount when the total quantity meets a threshold. __init__ validates its arguments: it requires base to be a PricingStrategy (TypeError otherwise), threshold to be a positive int via ensure_positive_int, and percent_off to be an int in 0..100 (TypeError or ValueError on invalid inputs), and stores them. Properties threshold and percent_off return the configured threshold and discount percent. price is not implemented yet; based on its name and the class purpose it should compute the base strategy total for a sequence of LineItem objects, check the total quantity against the threshold, and return a Money value that applies percent_off to the base total when the threshold is met. __repr__ returns a developer-friendly representation showing threshold and percent_off.
playground/playground/repository.py::000: Defines InMemoryRepository, a dict-backed implementation of Repository restricted to a specific entity type. The constructor __init__(entity_type) validates that entity_type is a type and initializes an internal dict; it raises TypeError if given a non-type. add(item) validates the item is an instance of the repository's entity type, computes its identity() as the key, raises DuplicateEntityError if the key already exists, and stores the item; wrong-type items raise TypeError. get(key) requires a string key, raises TypeError for non-strings and KeyError if missing, and returns the stored Entity. remove(key) raises KeyError if key is missing and returns and removes the entity. __contains__(key) returns True only for string keys present in the store. __len__() returns the count of stored entities. __iter__() yields stored entities in order of sorted keys.
playground/playground/simulation.py::000: This module defines a single module-level constant, _REPORT_KINDS, a tuple of strings ("created", "shipped", "cancelled", "rejected") representing the kinds of order reports the simulation produces. The rest of the file (lines shown) only contains imports of types and helpers used elsewhere in the package; it does not define any classes, functions, or additional executable logic. No validation, exceptions, or side effects are present in this excerpt.
playground/playground/simulation.py::001: Defines class SimulationReport, a plain container for counters and revenue from a simulation run. __init__ initializes internal counters for kinds found in _REPORT_KINDS and sets revenue to Money(0). Properties orders_created, orders_shipped, orders_cancelled, rejected_out_of_stock and revenue return the corresponding counts or Money total. record(kind) increments the counter for kind and raises ValueError if kind is not in _REPORT_KINDS. add_revenue(amount) adds a Money amount to the total, raising TypeError if amount is not a Money instance. summary() returns a dict of the counts and a formatted revenue string (using format_cents on the stored Money.cents), and __str__ renders that summary as one "key: value" line per entry.
playground/playground/simulation.py::002: Defines class Simulation with methods for driving random order activity against a Warehouse. __init__ binds a Warehouse and PricingStrategy to the simulation, performs type validation (raises TypeError if warehouse or pricing are wrong), initializes RNG, event bus, order log, report, next id counter and customer list. Properties log, report and bus return the respective internal objects. add_customer validates the argument as Customer (raises TypeError if not) and registers it. step() runs one simulation step and returns the created Order or None: it returns None immediately if there are no customers or no SKUs (recording a "rejected" report), randomly selects customer/sku/quantity, builds an order, attempts to reserve stock (catches OutOfStockError, records "rejected" and returns None), advances order status, records to the log/report, publishes events, uses the reservation context manager to optionally commit or let it roll back, may cancel with ~20% probability (records "cancelled" and publishes ORDER_CANCELLED) or ship (advances to SHIPPED, records revenue and publishes ORDER_SHIPPED). run(steps) validates steps via ensure_positive_int, runs that many step() calls, and returns the accumulated SimulationReport. Side effects include mutating the warehouse ledger via reservations/commits, updating the OrderLog and SimulationReport, publishing events on the EventBus, and advancing RNG and order id counter.
playground/playground/simulation.py::003: Defines two top-level functions. build_default_warehouse() creates an in-memory Product repository, adds three products (EL-1001, GR-2001, HW-3001) with categories and prices, constructs an InventoryLedger and a Warehouse ("WH-1", "Main"), receives 20 units of each SKU into the warehouse (updating inventory) and returns the Warehouse. run_simulation(seed: int, steps: int) validates that seed is an int (explicitly rejects bool) and raises TypeError otherwise, ensures steps is a positive int via ensure_positive_int, builds the default warehouse, instantiates a Simulation with FlatPricing(tax_bps=800) and the given seed, adds two Customer objects with specified balances, and returns the result of sim.run(steps) (a SimulationReport).
playground/playground/util.py::000: This module defines three helper functions. normalize_sku(raw: str) validates and normalises a SKU: it strips whitespace, uppercases the string, enforces length 3–16 and allows only ASCII uppercase letters, digits and hyphens, returning the normalized SKU; it raises TypeError if raw is not a str and ValueError for invalid length or characters. format_cents(cents: int) renders an integer cent amount as a "$X.YY" string, raising TypeError if cents is a bool or not an int and ValueError if cents is negative. ensure_positive_int(value, name) validates that value is an int (not a bool) and strictly greater than zero, returning the int or raising TypeError/ValueError with the parameter name included in the message.
playground/playground/util.py::001: Defines the function chunked(items, size) which yields successive lists of up to size elements taken from the iterable items. It validates size via ensure_positive_int(name="size") and will propagate TypeError or ValueError raised by that helper. chunked returns an iterator that yields full batches of exactly size items and a final smaller batch if there are leftover items; it yields no empty final batch. It has no other side effects.
playground/tests/test_base.py::000: This test module defines two small test helper classes, _Thing and _OtherThing, both subclassing Entity. Each class stores a string key passed to its constructor and implements identity() to return that key. There is no validation, exception raising, return values beyond identity(), and no side effects. These classes are intended for use in unit tests of the base module (e.g., to exercise Entity, PricingStrategy, and Repository behaviors) as simple concrete Entity implementations.
playground/tests/test_base.py::001: This chunk defines a unittest.TestCase subclass EntityTests that verifies behavior of an abstract Entity base and its concrete test doubles (_Thing and _OtherThing): test_is_abstract and test_subclass_without_identity_is_abstract assert that instantiating Entity or a subclass missing the required identity raises TypeError (abstract class). Several tests check equality and inequality semantics: same-type same-identity compares equal, different identity or different type compare unequal, comparisons with non-Entity return False, and __eq__ returns NotImplemented for mismatched entity types so Python falls back to identity. Hashing tests assert equal entities have equal hashes, that Entity instances are usable in sets, and that the hash incorporates the type name; repr is also checked. The chunk also defines a concrete _FlatPricing class inheriting PricingStrategy with price(self, items) implemented to return the sum of line-item subtotals via self._sum_subtotals(items).
playground/tests/test_base.py::002: PricingStrategyTests is a unittest.TestCase containing tests for the abstract PricingStrategy base: test_is_abstract asserts that instantiating PricingStrategy raises TypeError, test_call_delegates_to_price verifies that calling a concrete strategy (_FlatPricing) delegates to its price method and returns the expected Money total, and several tests verify the static/internal helper _sum_subtotals returns a Money instance, correctly sums LineItem subtotals for empty, single, multiple-item inputs and accepts a tuple input. The chunk also defines a simple in-memory repository class _DictRepository implementing Repository: __init__ initializes a dict storage, add stores an Entity by its identity, get returns an entity by key (KeyError if missing), remove pops and returns an entity, __iter__ yields stored Entity values, and __len__ returns the number of stored items.
playground/tests/test_base.py::003: RepositoryTests is a unittest.TestCase subclass containing unit tests for Repository behaviour. test_is_abstract asserts that instantiating Repository raises TypeError (it is abstract). test_contains_non_str_returns_false creates a _DictRepository, adds a _Thing("a"), and asserts that non-string membership checks (an int and a _Thing instance) return False. test_contains_present_key_is_true verifies that a string key present in the repository ("a") is reported as in the repository. test_contains_missing_key_is_false_via_keyerror checks that a missing string key yields False without raising. test_contains_uses_get defines a _Spy subclass that overrides get to record the key, confirms "k" is reported present, and asserts that get was called with "k", verifying that __contains__ delegates to get.
playground/tests/test_decorators.py::000: These are unit tests for the AuditTrail class imported from playground.decorators. The tests verify that constructing AuditTrail() with no arguments creates an empty trail (len returns 0 and entries is an empty tuple), that a custom string label like "ops" is accepted, that passing a non-string label (e.g. integer) raises TypeError, and that providing an empty or all-whitespace string label raises ValueError. The suite exercises only construction/validation behavior and does not test any other methods or side effects.
playground/tests/test_decorators.py::001: AuditTrailCallTests contains unit tests for the AuditTrail decorator/callable wrapper. The tests check that calling AuditTrail with a non-callable raises TypeError, that a successful wrapped function returns its result and appends an "audit:name:ok" entry, and that a wrapped function that raises an exception re-raises it and records an "audit:name:error:ExceptionClass" entry. They verify the wrapper preserves function metadata (__name__ and __doc__), correctly forwards positional and keyword arguments, accumulates entries in call order (and updates __len__), and can be shared by multiple functions. Finally, they assert that subclasses of BaseException (KeyboardInterrupt) are not caught and are not recorded.
playground/tests/test_decorators.py::002: AuditTrailEntriesClearTests is a unittest.TestCase subclass containing four tests that exercise the AuditTrail decorator/collection behavior. test_entries_is_snapshot_tuple verifies that AuditTrail.entries returns an immutable snapshot tuple (so a later call to the decorated function appends to the trail but does not change the previously grabbed snapshot) and checks recorded entry strings like "a:f:ok". test_clear_empties confirms that AuditTrail.clear() removes all entries, that len(trail) becomes 0 and entries becomes an empty tuple. test_clear_on_empty_is_noop ensures calling clear() on an already empty trail does nothing and keeps length 0. test_recording_resumes_after_clear checks that after clear() the trail resumes recording new entries. The module also runs the tests when executed as __main__.
playground/tests/test_enums.py::000: Defines a unittest.TestCase subclass CategoryTests that contains unit tests for the Category enum from playground.enums. The tests verify that each Category member has the expected .value strings, that Category.from_label returns the correct enum member for exact matches and when input is trimmed and case-normalized, and that from_label resolves every member when given its value. The tests also assert that from_label raises TypeError for non-str inputs, raises ValueError for unknown or empty-string labels (and that the unknown-label error message contains "unknown category" and the original input), and that str(member) returns the member's .value. EventType and OrderStatus are imported but not used in these tests.
playground/tests/test_enums.py::001: This test module defines two unittest.TestCase subclasses that exercise enum types: OrderStatusTests verifies that OrderStatus members have the expected string values for NEW, RESERVED, SHIPPED, and CANCELLED, and checks the is_terminal boolean property for each member (asserting SHIPPED and CANCELLED are terminal and NEW and RESERVED are not). EventTypeTests verifies the integer values of EventType members STOCK_ADDED, STOCK_RESERVED, STOCK_RELEASED, ORDER_SHIPPED, and ORDER_CANCELLED. It also checks that EventType members are hashable and distinct by asserting that a set of EventType yields length 5. The file runs the tests when executed as __main__.
playground/tests/test_events.py::000: This file defines a unittest.TestCase subclass EventBusSubscribeTests that exercises the EventBus.subscribe, __len__, and containment behavior. setUp creates a fresh EventBus for each test. test_starts_empty asserts the bus initially has length 0 and does not contain EventType.STOCK_ADDED. test_subscribe_registers_handler verifies that subscribing a callable to an EventType increases len and makes that event type present. test_subscribe_non_event_type_rejected and test_subscribe_non_callable_rejected assert that subscribing with a non-EventType or a non-callable raises TypeError. test_same_handler_twice_counted_twice and test_len_sums_across_types check that duplicate subscriptions are counted separately and that __len__ sums handlers across different event types.
playground/tests/test_events.py::001: This test module defines the EventBusUnsubscribeTests unittest.TestCase which sets up a fresh EventBus in setUp. test_unsubscribe_registered_returns_true verifies that subscribing a handler and then unsubscribing it returns True and that the bus length drops to zero. test_unsubscribe_unknown_handler_returns_false and test_unsubscribe_on_unknown_type_returns_false check that attempting to unsubscribe a handler that was never registered (or from an event type with no handlers) returns False. test_unsubscribe_wrong_type_returns_false ensures unsubscribing the same handler from a different event type does not remove it and returns False, leaving the subscription count unchanged. test_unsubscribe_removes_first_occurrence_only confirms that if the same handler was subscribed twice, unsubscribe removes only the first occurrence (bus length decreases by one) and subsequent publish calls invoke the handler once.
playground/tests/test_events.py::002: EventBusPublishTests is a unittest.TestCase that exercises the EventBus.publish behavior. setUp creates an EventBus and a received list; test_publish_no_handlers_returns_zero asserts publish returns 0 when there are no handlers. test_publish_calls_handler_with_payload subscribes a handler and checks publish returns the number of handlers invoked and that the handler receives the exact payload; test_publish_only_matching_type ensures handlers for other event types are not called. test_handlers_called_in_subscription_order verifies handlers run in subscription order. test_publish_non_event_type_rejected and test_publish_non_mapping_payload_rejected assert publish raises TypeError for an invalid event type or non-Mapping payload, while test_publish_accepts_any_mapping shows any Mapping (e.g. MappingProxyType) is allowed. test_handler_exception_propagates checks exceptions raised by handlers propagate out of publish, and test_handler_unsubscribing_during_publish_does_not_skip verifies a handler that unsubscribes itself during publish does not prevent subsequent handlers from being called and the publish still counts both calls.
playground/tests/test_events.py::003: Defines a unittest.TestCase subclass EventBusContainsTests that verifies membership behavior of EventBus (i.e., its __contains__ implementation). test_contains_false_without_handlers asserts that a fresh EventBus does not contain EventType.ORDER_SHIPPED. test_contains_true_with_handler subscribes a lambda handler for EventType.ORDER_SHIPPED and asserts the event type is then contained. test_contains_false_after_all_unsubscribed subscribes and then unsubscribes a handler and asserts the event type is no longer contained. test_contains_non_event_type_is_false asserts non-EventType values ("ORDER_SHIPPED" string and integer 4) are not considered contained. The file ends with a unittest.main() call to run the tests when executed as a script.
playground/tests/test_exceptions.py::000: This file defines a unittest.TestCase subclass ExceptionHierarchyTests with multiple test methods that validate the exception class hierarchy imported from playground.exceptions. Each test method (e.g., test_root_derives_from_exception, test_inventory_error_derives_from_root, test_out_of_stock_derives_from_inventory_error, test_unknown_sku_derives_from_inventory_error, test_duplicate_entity_derives_from_root_only, test_invalid_transition_derives_from_root_only) asserts specific issubclass relationships between PlaygroundError, InventoryError, OutOfStockError, UnknownSKUError, DuplicateEntityError, and InvalidTransitionError, including negative checks that DuplicateEntityError and InvalidTransitionError do not derive from InventoryError. test_every_class_is_playground_error_subclass checks that exactly six named classes exist and all are subclasses of PlaygroundError. test_root_catches_all_subclasses verifies that raising instances of each concrete exception can be caught as PlaygroundError.
playground/tests/test_exceptions.py::001: This test module defines four unittest.TestCase subclasses that verify custom exception classes' behavior. OutOfStockErrorTests checks that OutOfStockError stores sku, requested and available attributes, formats its string message as "insufficient stock for {sku}: requested {requested}, available {available}", and is catchable as the broader InventoryError. UnknownSKUErrorTests asserts UnknownSKUError stores sku and formats as "unknown SKU: {sku}". DuplicateEntityErrorTests asserts DuplicateEntityError stores key and formats as "duplicate entity: {key}". InvalidTransitionErrorTests verifies InvalidTransitionError stores source and target, formats as "invalid transition: '{source}' -> '{target}'", and accepts arbitrary (non-string) objects for source/target. The module runs the tests when executed as __main__.
playground/tests/test_inventory.py::000: This file defines a helper function _make_repo and a unittest.TestCase subclass InventoryLedgerConstructionTests with two test methods. _make_repo creates and returns an InMemoryRepository pre-populated with two Product instances (an electronics and a grocery item) priced with Money. test_requires_repository verifies that constructing InventoryLedger with an invalid argument type (a dict) raises a TypeError. test_accepts_repository verifies that constructing InventoryLedger with a valid repository returned by _make_repo succeeds and that the newly created ledger has length 0. The tests therefore check constructor argument validation and initial empty-state behavior of InventoryLedger.
playground/tests/test_inventory.py::001: InventoryLedgerStockTests is a unittest.TestCase that sets up an InventoryLedger backed by _make_repo() and contains tests for InventoryLedger.add_stock, InventoryLedger.available, and the internal helper _require_sku. The tests verify that add_stock returns the new on-hand total and normalizes/skips surrounding whitespace in SKUs, raises UnknownSKUError (with sku attribute) for unknown SKUs, raises ValueError for malformed SKU characters or zero quantity, and raises TypeError for boolean quantities; they also assert quantity validation occurs before SKU validation. Tests for available check that it defaults to zero when no stock, raises UnknownSKUError for unknown SKUs, and normalizes input. Tests for _require_sku assert it returns an uppercase/trimmed SKU, raises UnknownSKUError for unknown SKUs, and raises ValueError for malformed SKUs.
playground/tests/test_inventory.py::002: InventoryLedgerReserveTests is a unittest.TestCase that sets up an InventoryLedger with 10 units of SKU "EL-1001" in setUp. test_reserve_returns_context_and_reduces_available verifies reserve returns a ReservationContext in state "held" and reduces available quantity accordingly. test_reserve_exact_available_allowed confirms reserving the exact available amount yields zero available. test_reserve_over_available_raises_out_of_stock and test_reserve_considers_existing_reservations check that reserving more than available raises OutOfStockError with sku, requested and available attributes reflecting current stock and existing reservations. test_reserve_unknown_sku asserts UnknownSKUError is raised for unknown SKUs, test_reserve_bad_quantity asserts type and value validation for quantity, and test_reserve_out_of_stock_on_unstocked_sku checks OutOfStockError reports zero available for unstocked SKUs.
playground/tests/test_inventory.py::003: InventoryLedgerReleaseCommitTests is a unittest.TestCase that sets up an InventoryLedger with SKU "EL-1001" and 10 units on hand before each test. It tests release behavior: releasing reserved quantity restores available stock and partial releases reduce reserved appropriately, releasing more than reserved or releasing when nothing is reserved raises InvalidTransitionError (the exception records source and target), releasing an unknown SKU raises UnknownSKUError, and releasing a non-positive quantity raises ValueError. It also tests commit behavior: committing reduces both on_hand and reserved counts (fully or partially), committing more than reserved or when nothing is reserved raises InvalidTransitionError (with source/target checked), committing an unknown SKU raises UnknownSKUError, and passing a non-integer quantity raises a TypeError. The tests inspect available(), and internal _on_hand and _reserved mappings to verify side effects.
playground/tests/test_inventory.py::004: InventoryLedgerContainsLenIterTests is a unittest.TestCase that constructs an InventoryLedger in setUp and exercises its membership (__contains__), length (__len__) and iteration (__iter__) behaviors via the public methods add_stock, reserve and commit. Tests verify that membership returns False for non-string keys and malformed strings, that input is normalized so " el-1001 " is recognized after add_stock, that an unstocked but valid SKU is not contained, and that a SKU can still be considered contained after being fully committed because its key remains. Length counts only SKUs with positive on-hand quantities and excludes fully committed (zeroed) SKUs. Iteration yields a sorted list of SKUs, skips SKUs with zero on-hand, and yields an empty list when no positive stock exists.
playground/tests/test_inventory.py::005: ReservationContextTests is a unittest.TestCase that sets up an InventoryLedger with 10 units of "EL-1001" and exercises the ReservationContext returned by ledger.reserve. It verifies that a fresh ReservationContext starts in state "held", that entering the context manager returns the same ReservationContext instance, and that exiting the context without calling commit releases the held stock back to available. It checks that calling commit inside the with-block marks the context "committed" and permanently consumes the reserved stock (reflected in available() and the ledger's _on_hand). It also asserts that exceptions raised inside the with-block both release the reservation and propagate, and that the context manager's __exit__ returns False.
playground/tests/test_inventory.py::006: ReservationContextTests is a unittest.TestCase that exercises the ReservationContext returned by ledger.reserve(item_sku, qty). The tests verify __exit__ behavior: when a reservation has been committed, __exit__(None,None,None) returns False and does not change available inventory, and calling __exit__ a second time after an earlier release is a no-op. They check context manager/transition validation: entering after a release raises InvalidTransitionError with source "released" and target "held", entering after commit raises InvalidTransitionError, committing twice raises InvalidTransitionError with source and target both "committed", and committing after a release raises InvalidTransitionError. Finally, repr(rc) is asserted to show the SKU, quantity, and current state ("held" or "committed").
playground/tests/test_inventory.py::007: Defines two unittest.TestCase classes that exercise Warehouse and inventory error behavior. WarehouseTests sets up an InventoryLedger and a Warehouse and tests Warehouse.identity(), that the .ledger property returns the ledger, and that invalid IDs (empty or non-str) or a non-ledger third argument raise ValueError/TypeError. It verifies receive delegates to the ledger and returns updated on-hand counts, that receiving an unknown SKU raises UnknownSKUError and receiving a nonpositive quantity raises ValueError, that stock_report() returns available quantities (accounting for reservations) or {} when empty, repr formatting, and equality by warehouse id. InventoryErrorHierarchyTests checks that attempting to reserve an out-of-stock SKU raises the base InventoryError.
playground/tests/test_models.py::000: This test module defines a unittest.TestCase subclass MoneyConstructionTests that contains unit tests for the Money model. The tests verify that Money() defaults to zero cents and that Money(n) stores the provided integer cents value. Several tests assert input validation: passing a bool, float, or str raises TypeError, passing a negative integer raises ValueError with the message "money cannot be negative", and attempting to assign to the cents attribute raises AttributeError to ensure cents is read-only. Collectively the tests check construction, type and value validation, error messages, and immutability of the cents attribute.
playground/tests/test_models.py::001: MoneyArithmeticTests is a unittest.TestCase that tests arithmetic behaviour of a Money class. It verifies Money.__add__ accepts only Money and returns a new Money with summed value, raising TypeError for non-Money addition. It verifies Money.__sub__ accepts only Money, allows zero results, but raises ValueError when the result would be negative and TypeError for non-Money subtraction. It verifies Money.__mul__ accepts only non-boolean ints (rejecting bool and float) and non-negative factors, returning a new Money with scaled value (including zero). It also tests __rmul__ supports ints on the left, delegates to __mul__, and raises TypeError for invalid left operands.
playground/tests/test_models.py::002: MoneyComparisonTests is a unittest.TestCase that exercises comparison behavior of the Money class. It tests __eq__ for equal and unequal cents values, verifies that comparing to non-Money via the operator returns False while the special method __eq__ returns NotImplemented for non-Money, and checks __ne__ behavior. It validates ordering: __lt__ works for less-than and returns NotImplemented when called with non-Money but raises TypeError when using the < operator against non-Money; __gt__ is checked via Python's reflected resolution from __lt__. It similarly tests __le__ and __ge__ (with __ge__ coming from reflection of __le__), and ensures Money instances can be sorted using their cents values.
playground/tests/test_models.py::003: MoneyMiscTests is a unittest.TestCase containing unit tests for the Money class. It checks hashing behavior, asserting that hash(Money(7)) equals hash(Money(7)) and also equals hash(("Money", 7)), implying Money.__hash__ produces the same value as that tuple. It tests that Money instances can be used in sets by verifying {Money(1), Money(1), Money(2)} has length 2. It asserts repr(Money(1234)) == "Money(1234)" and that str formats amounts as dollars ("$12.34" for 1234 and "$0.00" for 0). Finally it verifies truthiness: Money(0) is falsey while Money(1) is truthy.
playground/tests/test_models.py::004: ProductTests is a unittest.TestCase subclass that defines a helper _make(...) to construct Product instances with default fields (sku, name, category, unit_price) overridable via kwargs. The tests check that Product is an Entity, that the constructor stores sku, name, category and unit_price correctly, and that sku strings are normalized (e.g., " el-1001 " -> "EL-1001"). Several tests verify validation and error propagation: invalid sku values raise ValueError, non-str sku raises TypeError, missing or blank name raises ValueError with message "name required" for None, non-Category category raises TypeError, and non-Money unit_price raises TypeError. Additional tests assert Product properties are read-only (assigning raises AttributeError) and that identity() returns the sku.
playground/tests/test_models.py::005: ProductTests is a unittest.TestCase containing unit tests for the Product model. test_equality_by_identity_same_sku_different_name asserts Products compare equal when their SKUs match (case-normalized) even if names differ, while test_inequality_different_sku asserts inequality for different SKUs. test_with_price_returns_new_product verifies Product.with_price returns a new Product (no in-place mutation), preserves sku, name and category identity, and updates unit_price; test_with_price_non_money_rejected asserts calling with_price with a non-Money value raises a TypeError. test_from_dict_with_category_string and test_from_dict_with_category_enum verify Product.from_dict accepts either a category name string or a Category enum, normalizes SKU casing, and converts unit_price_cents to a Money instance.
playground/tests/test_models.py::006: ProductTests is a unittest.TestCase that verifies Product.from_dict and Product.is_valid_name behaviours. The from_dict tests check that omitting any required key ("sku", "name", "category", "unit_price_cents") raises a KeyError whose .args[0] equals the missing key (using subTest for each key), that a non-string category raises TypeError, an unknown category label raises ValueError, a negative unit_price_cents raises ValueError, and a non-integer price (float) raises TypeError. The is_valid_name tests assert that normal names are accepted, non-string inputs and blank or all-whitespace strings are rejected, name length is allowed from 1 up to 80 characters but not 81, and that surrounding whitespace is stripped before measuring length.
playground/tests/test_models.py::007: LineItemTests is a unittest.TestCase class that exercises the LineItem model. The tests verify that LineItem stores and (apparently) normalizes fields (constructing LineItem("el-1001", 2, Money(250)) yields sku "EL-1001"), exposes a subtotal property that multiplies quantity by unit_price, and propagates SKU validation errors as ValueError. They assert quantity validation: passing a bool raises TypeError with message "quantity must be int", zero or negative quantities raise ValueError, and non-Money unit_price raises TypeError. The tests also check that with_quantity returns a new LineItem (immutability) with the updated quantity and preserved unit_price, and that with_quantity performs the same type/value validation (rejecting non-int and zero).
playground/tests/test_models.py::008: LineItemTests is a unittest.TestCase containing unit tests for the LineItem model's equality, hashing, and representation behavior. It tests that two LineItem instances with the same SKU (case-insensitively), quantity and Money price compare equal, and that differing quantity or price make them unequal. It verifies that LineItem.__eq__ returns NotImplemented when comparing to a non-LineItem (so the == expression yields False). It also checks that equal LineItem objects have equal hashes and that the hash matches the tuple ("EL-1001", 1), and that repr(LineItem(...)) produces "LineItem('EL-1001', 2, Money(250))".
playground/tests/test_models.py::009: CustomerTests is a unittest.TestCase class that exercises the Customer model. The tests verify that a newly created Customer defaults credit_limit and balance to Money(0), that the constructor stores customer_id, name and credit_limit correctly and that Customer instances are subclasses of Entity. They check value semantics of the default credit_limit (equal across instances), validate input by asserting ValueError for empty or non-string customer_id/name and TypeError when credit_limit is not a Money, and assert that identity() returns the customer_id. Finally, equality is tested to be based on customer_id (same id => equal, different id => not equal).
playground/tests/test_models.py::010: CustomerTests is a unittest.TestCase subclass that tests the Customer model's affordability and charging behavior. The tests assert that Customer.can_afford returns True when a purchase amount is within the customer's credit limit and False when it exceeds the limit, that can_afford accounts for the customer's existing balance, and that passing a non-Money argument to can_afford raises TypeError. The tests also verify that Customer.charge increases the customer's balance correctly, that charging more than the credit limit raises ValueError with the message "credit limit exceeded" while leaving the balance unchanged, that charging exactly to the limit is allowed, and that passing a non-Money argument to charge raises TypeError. Finally, the tests confirm the balance attribute is read-only by asserting assignment to balance raises AttributeError.

playground/tests/test_orders.py::001: OrderStateMachineTests is a unittest.TestCase subclass that exercises the OrderStateMachine API and its error handling. The tests check that can_transition allows NEW->RESERVED and NEW->CANCELLED, disallows NEW->SHIPPED and RESERVED->NEW, allows RESERVED->SHIPPED and RESERVED->CANCELLED, and that terminal states (SHIPPED, CANCELLED) have no outgoing transitions. allowed_from is expected to return a frozenset of allowed target OrderStatus values, raise TypeError for non-OrderStatus input, and return an empty frozenset for terminal states. transition should return the target OrderStatus when legal and raise InvalidTransitionError (whose exception instance exposes .source and .target) for illegal transitions, and __call__ on the state machine is tested as an alias for transition.
playground/tests/test_orders.py::002: OrderConstructionTests is a unittest.TestCase containing tests for Order construction and basic properties. test_initial_state constructs an order via helper _order("ORD-9") and asserts the order_id is "ORD-9", the attached customer's customer_id is "C-1", the status is OrderStatus.NEW, items is an empty tuple, and len(o) == 0. test_empty_order_id_rejected and test_non_str_order_id_rejected assert the Order constructor raises ValueError for blank or non-string order_id. test_non_customer_rejected and test_non_pricing_rejected assert the constructor raises TypeError when given a non-customer or non-pricing argument. test_customer_property checks that Order.customer returns the same customer object passed in.
playground/tests/test_orders.py::003: OrderAddItemTests is a unittest.TestCase that sets up a fresh order in setUp via self.order = _order(). The tests verify Order.add_item behavior: test_add_appends_new_sku checks that adding two different LineItem objects appends both items and length and SKUs are correct; test_add_same_sku_merges_quantity ensures adding a LineItem with an existing SKU merges quantities rather than creating a new line; test_merge_keeps_position verifies merges do not change original item ordering. test_non_line_item_rejected asserts add_item rejects non-LineItem inputs by raising TypeError. test_add_after_advance_rejected and test_add_after_cancel_rejected assert that adding items after advancing to RESERVED or after CANCELLED raises InvalidTransitionError (the former test also checks the exception’s source is RESERVED and target is NEW).
playground/tests/test_orders.py::004: Defines two unittest.TestCase subclasses that test Order behavior. OrderAdvanceTests contains tests for the Order.advance method: it verifies valid transitions (NEW -> RESERVED -> SHIPPED), cancellation from NEW and RESERVED, that attempting an illegal transition (e.g., NEW -> SHIPPED) raises InvalidTransitionError and leaves the status unchanged, that advancing from a terminal status (CANCELLED) raises InvalidTransitionError, and that advancing to the same status raises InvalidTransitionError. OrderTotalTests checks the Order.total property: an empty order totals Money(0), the total uses a provided pricing strategy (FlatPricing adds a fee), and BulkDiscountPricing correctly merges line-item quantities for the same SKU and applies the bulk discount (asserting the discounted total equals Money(270)).
playground/tests/test_orders.py::005: OrderContainerTests is a unittest.TestCase that sets up an Order (via helper _order) with two LineItem entries and tests container behaviors: items returns a tuple snapshot (adding items afterwards does not change the previously obtained tuple), __len__ reports the number of items, iteration yields LineItem objects in order (tested via their skus), and iteration is a snapshot (an iterator created before adding an item yields only the original items). OrderEqualityTests is a unittest.TestCase that checks Order identity and representation: equality is based on order id and comparing to non-Order returns NotImplemented (so == with a non-Order is False), hashing is derived from ("Order", id) to allow set deduplication, and repr includes the order id and its status, which changes after calling advance(OrderStatus.CANCELLED).
playground/tests/test_orders.py::006: Defines a unittest.TestCase subclass OrderBuilderTests that exercises the OrderBuilder API. The tests check that OrderBuilder's constructor enforces argument types (raising TypeError for wrong types), that the classmethod for_customer returns an OrderBuilder (and preserves subclass typing) and uses FlatPricing for pricing (the built order has _pricing FlatPricing and total Money(1000)). They assert add returns self for chaining, validates inputs via LineItem (raising ValueError for bad SKU or zero quantity and TypeError for non-Money price) and does not add invalid items (len remains 0). add also normalizes SKUs (trims/uppercases), and build raises ValueError("no items") when called on an empty builder.
playground/tests/test_orders.py::007: OrderBuilderTests is a unittest.TestCase subclass containing unit tests for the OrderBuilder class. test_build_produces_order_with_lines verifies that building an order with two added lines returns an Order with the given order_id, NEW status, and correct total Money value. test_build_merges_duplicate_skus checks that adding the same SKU twice results in a single order line whose quantity is the sum of the added quantities. test_build_twice_creates_independent_orders ensures calling build twice produces independent Order objects (subsequent adds do not mutate previously built orders). test_build_propagates_bad_order_id asserts that building with an empty order id raises ValueError. test_len_and_bool verifies OrderBuilder implements __len__ and truthiness: empty builder has length 0 and is False, after adding a line length is 1 and it is True.
playground/tests/test_orders.py::008: OrderLogTests is a unittest.TestCase that sets up an OrderLog instance in setUp and tests its basic sequence and recording behaviour. It verifies that a fresh log is empty (len == 0 and iteration yields []), that record appends Order objects in insertion order and that __len__ and indexing reflect that order. Tests check that record rejects non-Order values with a TypeError and that recording a duplicate order id raises DuplicateEntityError whose .key equals the duplicated id while leaving the log unchanged. The tests also assert that __getitem__ supports negative indices, raises IndexError for out-of-range access, and that iteration yields items in insertion order with a snapshot copy taken when the iterator is first advanced.
playground/tests/test_orders.py::009: OrderLogTests is a set of unit tests for an OrderLog-like object (accessed as self.log) and its iteration and by_status functionality. test_iter_snapshot_isolated_after_first_next verifies that iter(self.log) yields a snapshot so that after consuming the first item and then recording a new order, the iterator still yields only the remaining pre-existing orders (checks order_id values). test_by_status_filters records three orders, advances two of them to different OrderStatus values, and asserts that by_status(status) yields only orders currently in that status and returns an empty list for a status with no matches. test_by_status_is_lazy_generator asserts by_status returns a lazy generator (no __len__) and that converting it to a list yields the expected contents. test_by_status_non_status_raises_on_first_next confirms that calling by_status with an invalid type (e.g. a string) does not raise immediately but raises TypeError when the generator is first advanced.

playground/tests/test_pricing.py::000: This test module defines a unittest.TestCase subclass FlatPricingConstructionTests that exercises construction and basic validation behavior of the FlatPricing class from the pricing module. The tests verify that the default tax_bps is 0 and that an explicit integer tax_bps (including boundary values 0 and 10000) is stored correctly. Finally, one test checks that FlatPricing instances implement the PricingStrategy interface. The file imports BulkDiscountPricing, LineItem, and Money but does not test them here.
playground/tests/test_pricing.py::001: FlatPricingPriceTests is a unittest.TestCase that tests the pricing behaviour of the FlatPricing strategy (using Money and LineItem fixtures). The tests verify that pricing an empty list of items returns Money(0) both with and without a tax rate, that a zero tax returns the raw subtotal, and that tax is computed from basis points as integer cents using floor division (so taxes round down). It also checks that a 10000 bps tax doubles the amount and that calling the strategy object is equivalent to calling its price(items) method. No exceptions are tested.
playground/tests/test_pricing.py::002: This test class exercises construction and basic properties of BulkDiscountPricing. It verifies that the constructor stores the threshold and percent_off fields, that the base argument must be a pricing strategy (otherwise TypeError), and that threshold is validated (zero raises ValueError, boolean threshold raises TypeError). It asserts percent_off rejects booleans and floats with TypeError, rejects negative values and values >100 with ValueError, and accepts the boundary values 0 and 100. It also checks that repr produces "BulkDiscountPricing(threshold=5, percent_off=10)" and that BulkDiscountPricing instances are instances of PricingStrategy.
playground/tests/test_pricing.py::003: This test module defines BulkDiscountPriceTests, a unittest.TestCase class that exercises the BulkDiscountPricing pricing wrapper (used with LineItem, Money and FlatPricing). The tests verify that BulkDiscountPricing.price returns the base total when total quantity is below the threshold and applies the specified percentage discount when quantity meets or exceeds the threshold, that quantities are summed across multiple line items, and that a zero-percent discount returns the base total while a 100% discount yields zero. Tests also assert the discount uses floor (integer) division when computing the discount amount, that BulkDiscountPricing applies its discount to whatever value the wrapped FlatPricing produces (e.g., after tax), that empty item lists return Money(0), and that calling the object (d(items)) delegates to price(items).

InMemoryRepositoryConstructionTests.test_is_repository asserts that InMemoryRepository(Product) is an instance of the abstract Repository type. test_non_type_rejected asserts that passing a non-type (a string) to InMemoryRepository raises TypeError, and test_new_repo_is_empty asserts a newly constructed InMemoryRepository(_Item) has length zero.
playground/tests/test_repository.py::001: InMemoryRepositoryAddTests is a unittest.TestCase that sets up an InMemoryRepository parameterized for _Item in setUp. test_add_then_get verifies that adding an _Item stores it so repo.get(key) returns the exact object and len(repo) becomes 1. test_add_wrong_type_rejected and test_add_non_entity_rejected assert that adding an object of the wrong class or a non-entity raises TypeError (the former’s message must mention "_Item"). test_add_duplicate_raises checks that adding a second entity with the same key raises DuplicateEntityError, that the exception exposes the duplicate key, and that repository size remains unchanged. test_duplicate_check_keeps_original ensures the original stored instance is preserved after a duplicate-add attempt. test_subclass_instances_accepted confirms instances of _Item subclasses are accepted and their keys appear in the repository.
playground/tests/test_repository.py::002: This test file defines two unittest.TestCase classes that exercise InMemoryRepository behavior. playground/tests/test_repository.py::003: This test module defines two unittest.TestCase classes that exercise InMemoryRepository behavior. playground/tests/test_simulation.py::001: SimulationReportTests is a unittest.TestCase class that tests the behaviour of the SimulationReport class. The tests verify that a new SimulationReport defaults numeric counters to zero and revenue to Money(0); that record(kind) increments the correct counter for "created", "shipped", "cancelled" and "rejected" (with "rejected" accumulating counts); and that record raises ValueError for unknown kinds and is case-sensitive. The add_revenue method is checked to accumulate Money values and to raise TypeError if given a non-Money argument. summary() is expected to return a dict with counters and a formatted revenue string like "$12.34" (and "$0.00" when zero), and str(report) must produce a multiline summary containing lines such as "orders_created: 1" and "revenue: $0.00".
playground/tests/test_simulation.py::002: SimulationConstructionTests is a unittest.TestCase containing tests for Simulation construction and basic behavior. test_warehouse_type_checked and test_pricing_type_checked verify the Simulation constructor enforces types by raising TypeError for invalid warehouse or pricing arguments. test_creates_default_bus_and_collaborators checks a newly constructed Simulation creates default collaborators: an EventBus assigned to sim.bus, an OrderLog assigned to sim.log, and a SimulationReport assigned to sim.report, and that the log is initially empty. test_uses_supplied_bus verifies a supplied EventBus instance is used as sim.bus. test_no_customers_step_returns_none asserts that calling sim.step() with no customers returns None and that the report shows zero orders_created and zero rejected_out_of_stock. test_add_customer_non_customer_rejected asserts sim.add_customer raises TypeError when given a non-Customer.
playground/tests/test_simulation.py::003: SimulationStepTests defines a helper method _sim(seed, warehouse) that builds a Simulation with a default (or provided) Warehouse, flat pricing, and a seeded RNG, and adds a single customer; it returns the Simulation. test_no_stock_records_rejected_and_returns_none reserves all available inventory in the warehouse, calls sim.step(), and asserts that step() returns None and the simulation report increments rejected_out_of_stock. test_empty_ledger_no_skus_records_rejected constructs a Warehouse with an InventoryLedger backed by an in-memory Product repository containing one product (but no stock), asserts sim.step() returns None and rejected_out_of_stock is incremented. test_step_returns_order_and_accounts_for_it calls step(), checks it returns an Order whose status is either SHIPPED or CANCELLED, and verifies the simulation log length and report counters (orders_created and either orders_shipped or orders_cancelled). test_order_ids_are_sequential verifies that successive calls to step() produce Orders with sequential order_id values ("ORD-00001", "ORD-00002").
playground/tests/test_simulation.py::004: SimulationStepTests defines unit tests for the simulation step behavior via three test methods. test_order_line_has_unit_price_1000_and_quantity_1_to_3 creates a simulator with a fixed seed, runs one step, asserts exactly one order was produced, that the first order line has unit_price Money(1000) and quantity in (1,2,3). test_shipped_path_publishes_and_adds_revenue subscribes to ORDER_SHIPPED, STOCK_RESERVED and ORDER_CANCELLED events on the simulator bus, runs steps until a shipped order appears (failing if none within 40 attempts), and asserts that reserved and shipped events were published in order, no cancelled event occurred after a reservation, and that report.revenue increased. test_cancel_path_releases_reservation builds a default warehouse and runs up to 200 steps, asserting after every step that no reservations remain held, that when a cancelled order appears it did not reduce on-hand stock, and that report.orders_cancelled was incremented; it fails if no cancelled order is produced. The tests rely on helper _sim and build_default_warehouse and will fail if expected events or state invariants are not met.
playground/tests/test_simulation.py::005: SimulationStepTests is a unittest.TestCase subclass containing tests for one-step behavior of the Simulation. test_rejected_when_reserve_fails stubs the warehouse ledger.reserve to always raise playground.exceptions.OutOfStockError and asserts that sim.step() returns None, increments sim.report.rejected_out_of_stock by 1, and produces no log entries. test_reserved_event_payload_fields subscribes to the EventType.STOCK_RESERVED event, runs one step, and asserts exactly one event was published whose payload contains order_id, sku, and quantity that match the reserved order. test_terminal_event_published_once_per_step subscribes to ORDER_SHIPPED and ORDER_CANCELLED events and verifies exactly one terminal event is published per step by checking five steps produce five terminal notifications. test_same_seed_is_reproducible runs repeated simulations with the same RNG seed and asserts the sequence of order status values is identical between runs.
playground/tests/test_simulation.py::006: This chunk defines two unittest.TestCase subclasses that exercise Simulation.run and the build_default_warehouse helper. SimulationRunTests checks that Simulation.run raises ValueError for n=0 and TypeError for non-integer inputs, and that a valid run returns the simulation's report object whose summed orders_shipped, orders_cancelled and rejected_out_of_stock equals the requested run count. BuildDefaultWarehouseTests verifies build_default_warehouse returns a Warehouse with identity "WH-1" and an initial stock report of 20 units each for SKUs "EL-1001", "GR-2001", "HW-3001", that those products have expected unit prices (2500, 300, 1200 respectively via the warehouse ledger), and that each call returns an independent Warehouse instance (reserving stock in one does not affect the other).
playground/tests/test_simulation.py::007: This test module defines the RunSimulationTests unittest.TestCase which exercises the run_simulation function and the SimulationReport it returns. Tests verify input validation: run_simulation raises TypeError if seed is a bool or non-int, raises TypeError if steps is non-int, and raises ValueError if steps is not positive. A functional test asserts run_simulation returns a SimulationReport, that the sum of orders_shipped, orders_cancelled and rejected_out_of_stock equals the requested number of steps, and that orders_created equals orders_shipped plus orders_cancelled. A determinism test asserts that calling run_simulation twice with the same seed and steps produces identical SimulationReport.summary() output.
playground/tests/test_util.py::000: Defines a unittest.TestCase subclass NormalizeSkuTests that exercises the normalize_sku function from playground.util. The tests verify that normalize_sku strips surrounding whitespace and uppercases input, enforces a post-strip length between 3 and 16 (raising ValueError with message "sku length must be 3..16" for too short or too long), and treats surrounding padding as not counting toward length. Several tests assert that non-str inputs raise TypeError, that invalid characters (underscore, inner space, punctuation, non-ASCII) raise ValueError (the underscore case expects the message "invalid sku characters"), and that digits and dashes are accepted (e.g., "123-456" remains "123-456").
playground/tests/test_util.py::001: FormatCentsTests is a unittest.TestCase subclass that tests the standalone function format_cents. The tests verify correct string formatting for various valid integer cent amounts: zero ("$0.00"), single-digit cents padded ("$0.05"), a typical amount ("$12.34"), whole dollars ("$1.00"), and a large amount ("$10000.00"). The suite also asserts input validation: boolean and float inputs and string inputs raise TypeError, and negative integers raise ValueError. Each invalid-case test uses subTest or assertRaises to check the appropriate exception is thrown.
playground/tests/test_util.py::002: EnsurePositiveIntTests is a unittest.TestCase that tests the behavior of the ensure_positive_int(value, name) function. It verifies that a positive integer is returned unchanged, that boolean values (True and False), floats, strings, and None raise TypeError (with True specifically producing the message "qty must be int"), and that zero and negative integers raise ValueError. It also checks that the ValueError for zero contains the message "steps must be positive". Overall the tests assert type validation and that only strictly positive ints are accepted.
playground/tests/test_util.py::003: This test class ChunkedTests (unittest.TestCase) exercises the chunked function, verifying that it splits iterables into consecutive lists of the requested size: even splits, a partial final chunk, when the requested size equals or exceeds the input length, when the input is empty, and when size is one. It asserts that each yielded chunk is a list and that chunked accepts generator inputs. The tests also validate error handling on invalid sizes: a size of zero or a negative integer causes the generator to raise ValueError on first next(), while a boolean or a float size causes a TypeError on first next(). The file ends by calling unittest.main() so the tests run when executed as a script.
